segments: Independent local business planning social posts
A solo newsletter writer, podcaster, or expert turning each long-form piece into posts for several social channels
The person responsible for social media at a small local business who needs a dependable schedule without losing room for timely posts
A small social media agency owner adding and removing client accounts as contracts change

business.what_it_does: Buffer is social media management software that helps small businesses and other users create, schedule, and publish posts, analyze performance, engage with comments, and collaborate across social channels.
business.business_model: Subscription software with a free plan and paid plans priced per connected social channel; paid plans can be billed monthly or yearly.

facts.statement: Buffer is made for small businesses and provides tools for scheduling posts, analyzing results, and engaging with their community.

provenance.quote: Buffer is a social media management software made for small businesses, providing the tools they need to schedule posts, analyze the results, and engage with their community.

facts.statement: Users can publish through Buffer's web application, mobile app, or browser extension.

provenance.quote: You can publish posts through our web application at buffer.com, through our mobile app, or through the browser extension.

facts.statement: Buffer supports publishing to Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube Shorts, Pinterest, Google Business, Mastodon, X, and Substack.

provenance.quote: Schedule your content to the most popular platforms including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube Shorts, Pinterest, Google Business, Mastodon, X and Substack.

facts.statement: The Create space helps users create, organize, and repurpose content and includes an AI Assistant.

provenance.quote: Whether you’re flying solo or working with a team, Buffer has all the features to help you create, organize, and repurpose your content for any channel. There’s also an AI Assistant if you need it.

facts.statement: The Community feature provides a single dashboard for triaging and responding to comments across channels.

provenance.quote: Engage with your audience across all your channels at 10x speed. Buffer will help you triage and respond to comments from one simple dashboard.

facts.statement: Insights provides single-channel and cross-channel analytics within the publishing dashboard.

provenance.quote: It's a lightweight analytics view built right into Buffer — check in on a single channel's follower growth, engagement, and impressions, or get a cross-channel overview of how all your channels are performing, all without ever leaving your publishing dashboard.

facts.statement: Insights includes period comparisons, post-performance rankings, follower-growth charts, tag filters, and AI-powered Takeaways.

provenance.quote: Features include summary metrics compared against an earlier period, a Performance per Post table you can sort to find your best content, follower growth charts, tag filters for tracking campaigns, and AI-powered Takeaways that suggest what to post next.

facts.statement: Paid plans can export Insights as CSV, Markdown, or branded PDF reports; chart snapshots are available on every plan, including Free.

provenance.quote: On our paid plans, you can also export your Insights as a CSV, Markdown, or branded PDF report. Chart snapshots can be downloaded on every plan, including Free.

facts.statement: Team collaboration includes access levels and approval workflows for creating, reviewing, and approving posts.

provenance.quote: Users with Approval Required access who will create posts for review by someone with Full Posting access on their team, and Owners, Admins, and users with Full Posting access who need to approve draft posts from team members with Approval Required access.

facts.statement: Start Page is a mobile-friendly landing page that users can build, update, and share across social profiles.

provenance.quote: It’s a simple, beautiful, flexible, mobile-friendly landing page that you can put together in minutes, update in seconds, and share across your social profiles.

facts.statement: The Free plan permits up to three simultaneous channel connections and imposes a lifetime limit of eight unique channels per social network.

provenance.quote: While our Free plan supports connections for up to three channels at once, there is a lifetime channel connection limit of 8 channels per social network.

facts.statement: Foster Coffee Company said Buffer enabled it to plan, schedule, and deliver content consistently while retaining flexibility for last-minute changes.

provenance.quote: Buffer is the ideal publishing platform for Foster because it enables them to plan, schedule and deliver their content in a consistent, yet flexible way.

entries.verbatim: If Buffer can't understand what you've typed, you'll see a small message below the search input suggesting examples. The message clears as soon as you keep editing your query or pick a supported format.

entries.claim: Custom and Last month date ranges are available on Essentials and Team plans.

entries.verbatim: - You can save any combination of date range and comparison as a named view — including the default **Last 30 days**, **Month to date**, **Last month**, **Last 7 days**, and **Custom**.

entries.claim: Reopening a saved view restores its date range and comparison.
entries.verbatim: Reopening the saved view restores both the date range and any comparison you had set.

entries.verbatim: The channel filter at the top of the Insights page drives every section on the page, including the Metrics chart. There's no separate in-chart channel picker.

entries.verbatim: 2. A dropdown will appear with a searchable list of your connected channels. 3. Check one or more channels to narrow Insights down to just those channels. You can also use **Select all** to include everything, or search by channel name to find one quickly.

entries.claim: Tags and Channel filters can be combined.
entries.verbatim: **Tip:** Tags and Channel filters can be used together so you can see how a specific content category performed across a subset of your channels.

entries.claim: Facebook Groups, Instagram personal profiles, and Start Page are excluded from Insights data and exports.
entries.verbatim: **Note: Insights doesn't support every channel type.** Facebook Groups, Instagram personal profiles, and Start Page are greyed out in the channel filter and excluded from Insights data and exports.

entries.claim: A channel group containing only unsupported channels is disabled in Insights.
entries.verbatim: If a channel group contains only unsupported channels, the whole group is disabled too.

entries.claim: Instagram and Facebook single-channel Insights views can be filtered by Post, Reel, or Story.
entries.verbatim: On the single-channel Insights page for Instagram and Facebook, you can filter your Insights by post type: Post, Reel, or Story.

entries.verbatim: 3. Check one or more types to narrow your Insights to just those formats. Leave everything unchecked to include every post type.

entries.verbatim: Smaller exports download almost immediately; larger ones (long date ranges or high post counts) may take a few minutes.

entries.claim: A spinner appears while an Insights export is being prepared.
entries.verbatim: A spinner will show while the file is being prepared so keep the tab open until the download starts.

entries.claim: PDF export configuration works the same on All Channels and single-channel Insights pages.
entries.verbatim: When you choose ***Export as PDF***, Buffer opens a short configuration step before the report generates. This works the same way on both the All Channels and single-channel Insights pages.

entries.claim: A PDF export can use a custom report name in its header or default to the organization name.
entries.verbatim: - **Report name**: a custom title shown in the PDF header. Leave it blank and Buffer will use your organization name instead.

entries.claim: A PDF export can replace default Buffer cover branding with an uploaded logo.
entries.verbatim: - **Cover logo**: upload your own logo to replace the default Buffer branding on the report's cover.

entries.claim: Buffer saves the last cover logo uploaded for reuse on the next PDF export.
entries.verbatim: Buffer saves the last logo you upload, so you won't need to re-upload it on your next export.

entries.claim: Every PDF report section is included by default and can be unchecked.
entries.verbatim: - **Sections to include**: every section is on by default. Uncheck anything you don't want in the final PDF.

entries.claim: The export configuration step applies only to PDF exports; CSV and Markdown exports begin immediately.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** This configuration step only applies to PDF exports. CSV and Markdown exports run immediately, with no extra step.

entries.claim: Insights exports include a Summary with each metric’s current value and percentage change versus the previous period.
entries.verbatim: - **Summary** — each metric's current value and its percentage change vs. the previous period.

entries.claim: Insights exports include one Performance per Post row per post, with identifying details, Buffer tags, and all available metrics for the channel.
entries.verbatim: - **Performance per Post** — one row per post, including Post ID, published date and time, a post excerpt, post type (image, reel, carousel, video, etc.), post URL, any Buffer tags applied, and all available metrics for that channel (impressions, reach, reactions, comments, shares, saves, engagement rate, and so on).

entries.claim: Insights exports include daily followers, posts published, and post views for the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - **Metrics Over Time** — daily followers, posts published, and post views for the selected period.

entries.claim: Exports include only the metrics reported by the channel and omit empty columns.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** Metrics included in the export vary by channel, just as they do in the Insights dashboard. You won't see empty columns — only the metrics your channel actually reports.

entries.claim: Each Insights export exactly reflects the filters currently applied.
entries.verbatim: **Tip:** If you want a different slice of your data, just update your filters and export again. Each export reflects the current state of your filters exactly.

entries.claim: The Summary shows channel performance for the selected date range compared with a chosen comparison period.
entries.verbatim: The Summary section gives you a snapshot of how your channel performed during the selected date range, compared to another period of your choice.

entries.claim: The default Previous Period comparison uses the same number of days immediately before the selected range.
entries.verbatim: - **Previous Period** — the same number of days immediately before your selected range (default).

entries.claim: Same Period Last Week compares with the equivalent calendar window one week earlier and is unavailable when the selected range exceeds 7 days.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Week** — the equivalent calendar window one week earlier. Best for short-range, week-over-week check-ins. (Unavailable when your selected date range is longer than 7 days.)

entries.claim: Same Period Last Month compares with the same calendar dates one month earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Month** — the same calendar dates one month back.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Year compares with the same calendar dates one year earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Year** — the same calendar dates one year back.

entries.claim: A Custom comparison uses a user-selected historical start date and a window equal in length to the current period; overlapping and future dates cannot be selected.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, can't be selected.

entries.claim: Each Summary metric updates its comparison indicator for the selected comparison period.
entries.verbatim: Each metric updates its comparison indicator (e.g. ↑ 28.6%) to reflect the period you've selected.

entries.claim: The Compare to dropdown is available only on single-channel Insights pages, not the All Channels view.
entries.verbatim: - The **Compare to** dropdown is currently available on single-channel Insights pages only. It does not appear on the All Channels view.

entries.claim: Bookmarked Insights views save both the comparison choice and date range.
entries.verbatim: - Your comparison choice is now saved alongside the date range when you bookmark a view, so reopening a saved view restores both.

entries.claim: The Followers table shows current followers and the exact number gained or lost during the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Followers table sits right at the top, showing your current followers and exactly how many you've gained (or lost) over your selected date range. We show that as a plain number, like +42, not a percentage, so you can see the real movement at a glance.

entries.claim: For networks that do not report follower counts daily, Insights displays the most recent reading available for the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - Some networks only check in on your follower count every so often instead of daily. When that's the case, you'll see the most recent reading available for your selected period.

entries.claim: The Followers table is hidden when a channel does not report follower data.
entries.verbatim: - If a channel doesn't report follower data at all, the Followers table will be hidden.

entries.claim: Insights reports the number of posts published during a period.
entries.verbatim: - **Posts** — the number of posts published during the period

entries.claim: Insights reports total likes or reactions received across all posts.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** — total likes/reactions received across all posts

entries.claim: Insights reports total comments received.
entries.verbatim: - **Comments** — total comments received

entries.claim: Insights reports total post displays as Impressions; for Instagram, this metric is labeled Views throughout Insights.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** — total number of times your posts were displayed. For Instagram, this metric is now labeled **Views** everywhere in Insights — on the single-channel page, the All Channels summary, and any mixed-channel selection that includes Instagram — matching what you see on Instagram's own Insights page.

entries.claim: Insights reports total shares.
entries.verbatim: - **Shares** — total shares

entries.claim: Insights reports total saves.
entries.verbatim: - **Saves** — total saves

entries.claim: Insights reports new followers gained during a period.
entries.verbatim: - **Follows** — new followers gained during the period

entries.claim: Insights reports Reach as the number of unique accounts that saw the content.
entries.verbatim: - **Reach** — the number of unique accounts that saw your content

entries.claim: Insights reports Engagement Rate as the percentage of viewers who engaged with the posts.
entries.verbatim: - **Engagement Rate** — the percentage of people who engaged with your posts out of those who saw them

entries.claim: Metric availability varies by channel according to data each social network shares through its API.
entries.verbatim: - Not all metrics are available for every channel — it depends on what each social network shares through its API. For example, Saves may only appear for Instagram, and Reach may not be available for all networks.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profiles, Reactions counts only reactions on the post itself.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** count only the reactions on the post itself, matching what you'd see on LinkedIn.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profiles, Comments includes nested replies under top-level comments.
entries.verbatim: - **Comments** include nested replies underneath top-level comments, since LinkedIn's own comment total works the same way.

entries.claim: LinkedIn Pages use a different API from LinkedIn profiles and do not break totals down in the same way.
entries.verbatim: - This applies to LinkedIn profile channels. LinkedIn Pages use a different LinkedIn API that doesn't break totals down the same way.

entries.claim: For Substack, Reactions counts likes on a Note and Comments counts replies.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** count likes on your Note, and **Comments** count replies.

entries.claim: For Substack, Restacks counts how many times a Note was restacked or reshared.
entries.verbatim: - **Restacks** count how many times someone restacked (reshared) your Note on Substack.

entries.claim: For Substack, Impressions counts every Note view and Reach counts unique viewers.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** count every time your Note was viewed, and **Reach** counts the unique people who viewed it.

entries.claim: For Substack, Shares counts clicks on a Note’s share link rather than restacks.
entries.verbatim: - **Shares** count clicks on your Note's share link, not restacks.

entries.claim: For Substack, Free Subscriptions and Paid Subscriptions count subscribers attributed by Substack to each Note.
entries.verbatim: - **Free Subscriptions** and **Paid Subscriptions** count the subscribers Substack attributes to each Note.

entries.claim: Engagement rate is unavailable for Substack because Substack does not provide the data required to calculate it.
entries.verbatim: - Engagement rate isn't available for Substack, because Substack doesn't share the numbers needed to calculate one.

entries.claim: Buffer does not provide Substack follower counts or publication-level statistics such as total subscribers and open rates.
entries.verbatim: - Follower counts and publication-level stats (like total subscribers or open rates) aren't available for Substack. Those stay in your Substack dashboard.

entries.claim: A single-channel Insights Summary can be turned into a ready-to-publish post.
entries.verbatim: On a single-channel Insights view, you can turn your Summary stats into a ready-to-publish post.

entries.claim: Share as Post generates a branded 1080×1080 image with top statistics, the channel avatar, and Buffer branding.
entries.verbatim: 2. This will generate a branded 1080×1080 image showing your top stats (reach, likes, replies, shares, etc.) with your channel's avatar and Buffer branding.

entries.claim: Share as Post opens the Post Composer with the generated image attached, alt text set, and a short caption pre-filled.
entries.verbatim: 3. Open the Post Composer with that image attached, alt text set, and a short caption pre-filled.

entries.claim: Users can edit the Share as Post copy, select channels, and schedule or publish the post.
entries.verbatim: 4. Tweak the copy, choose which channels to post to, and schedule or publish like any other post.

entries.claim: Share Summary is available only in single-channel Insights and does not appear in All Channels.
entries.verbatim: - **Share Summary is only available on single-channel Insights.** It doesn't appear on the All Channels view because there's no single channel for the post to default to.

entries.claim: Share Summary images always use a 1080×1080 square layout accepted by Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook without further cropping.
entries.verbatim: - The image always uses a 1080×1080 square layout, which Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook all accept without further cropping.

entries.claim: A Share Summary card shows up to 4 available statistics.
entries.verbatim: - Up to 4 stats are shown on the card, picked from what's available for your channel (reach, likes, replies, shares-style metrics).

entries.claim: Download Snapshots packages every chart’s Share-as-Post image into one ZIP without opening the composer.
entries.verbatim: 💡 **Tip:** Want to grab every chart's Share-as-Post image at once? Use ***Download Snapshots*** from the Export menu — it packages them all into a single ZIP without opening the composer.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots is available on every plan, including Free.
entries.verbatim: Available on every plan, including Free.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post table reports individual post performance for the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Performance per Post table breaks down how each individual post did during the selected date range.

entries.claim: For each post, Performance per Post can show a thumbnail and content preview, engagement rate, reactions, comments, and views.
entries.verbatim: **For each post, you'll see:** - **Post** — a thumbnail and preview of the post content - **Eng. Rate** — the engagement rate for that post - **Reactions** — the number of likes/reactions for that post - **Comments** - **Views**

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Views measures plays and Reach measures unique accounts that saw the Story.
entries.verbatim: - **Views**: how many times the Story was played. - **Reach**: the number of unique accounts that saw the Story.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Replies reports replies sent to the Story.
entries.verbatim: - **Replies**: replies sent to the Story.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, engagement rate is calculated as Interactions divided by Reach.
entries.verbatim: - **Eng. Rate**: engagement rate (Interactions ÷ Reach).

entries.claim: Users can rearrange Performance per Post columns with the column selector.
entries.verbatim: You can also rearrange the order of columns from the column selector, like this:

entries.claim: Users can sort the Performance per Post table by clicking a metric column header and reverse the order with a second click.
entries.verbatim: Click any metric column header in the Performance per Post table to sort by that metric. Click again to switch between descending and ascending order.

entries.claim: Sortable post metrics may include engagement rate, reactions, comments, views, impressions, reach, shares, reposts, clicks, saves, follows, quotes, total time watched, and viewers.
entries.verbatim: Sortable metrics may include Eng. **Rate, Reactions, Comments, Views, Impressions, Reach, Shares, Reposts, Clicks, Saves, Follows, Quotes, Total time watched,** and **Viewers.**

entries.claim: Sortable columns vary by network according to the metrics that network reports.
entries.verbatim: Sorting is per network. A column is only sortable where that channel actually reports the metric, so the sortable columns you see will vary by channel (for example, Facebook clicks are sortable on Facebook, and LinkedIn viewers and total time watched are sortable on LinkedIn).

entries.claim: Instagram Reels do not show a Follows column because Meta reports Follows only for Feed posts and Stories, not Reels.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** Some metrics also vary by post type. Instagram Reels, for example, don't show a Follows column, since Meta doesn't report Follows for Reels, only for Feed posts and Stories.

entries.claim: The Metrics section displays a line chart of a metric across the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Metrics section shows a line chart of a metric over your selected date range.

entries.claim: Date and tag filters do not affect the Metrics chart, which always displays the full year.
entries.verbatim: Note that date and tag filters do not apply to this chart — it always shows data for the full year regardless of the date range selected elsewhere in Insights.

entries.claim: A channel’s Metrics chart opens on Content Impact by default, combining posts with follower growth, and returns to Content Impact when switching channels.
entries.verbatim: When you open a channel, the chart opens on **Content Impact** by default, layering your posts on top of your follower growth so you can see how the two track together. Want a different view? Grab one from the buttons below. The default flips back to Content Impact each time you switch channels.

entries.claim: If a channel has no follower data, its Metrics chart opens on Posts instead of Content Impact.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** No follower data for a channel? The chart opens on **Posts** instead.

entries.claim: The Posts chart view shows publishing frequency during the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - **Posts** — how often you published during the selected period.

entries.claim: The Content Impact view displays post volume alongside follower growth.
entries.verbatim: - **Content Impact** — your post volume alongside follower growth, side by side.

entries.claim: The Audience Growth view displays followers over time and net new followers gained.
entries.verbatim: - **Audience Growth** — followers over time, plus net new followers gained.

entries.claim: The Visibility view compares impressions—or Views for Instagram—with follower count.
entries.verbatim: - **Visibility** — impressions (or Views, for Instagram) compared against your follower count.

entries.claim: Follower Growth Rate is a LinkedIn-only view that benchmarks monthly follower growth against similar Buffer accounts.
entries.verbatim: - **Follower Growth Rate** *(LinkedIn channels only)* — your monthly follower growth rate benchmarked against similar Buffer accounts. See the callout below for details.

entries.claim: Custom Metric Set is available on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: - **+ Custom Metric Set** (available on paid plans) — build your own view by selecting the metrics you want to track together.

entries.claim: Custom Metric Set lets users select metrics to track together in one view.
entries.verbatim: - **+ Custom Metric Set** (available on paid plans) — build your own view by selecting the metrics you want to track together.

entries.claim: The metric dropdown can switch the chart to any individual metric available for the channel.
entries.verbatim: Selecting a button updates the chart automatically. You can also use the **metric dropdown** (e.g. Followers) directly above the chart to switch to any individual metric available for your channel.

entries.claim: The Visibility tab appears only for networks that report views data and is hidden for Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon.
entries.verbatim: - The **Visibility** tab (impressions, or Views for Instagram) is only shown for networks that report views data. It's hidden on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon channels — those networks only report follower counts at the channel level, so there's no views data to display.

entries.claim: The LinkedIn Follower Growth Rate benchmark plots monthly growth over time, compares it with the median of similar Buffer accounts, and shows a percentile rank.
entries.verbatim: - The **Follower Growth Rate benchmark** is available on LinkedIn channels only. It plots your monthly follower growth rate over time and compares it against the median for a cohort of similar Buffer accounts, showing you a percentile rank so you can see where you stand relative to comparable pages.

entries.claim: The LinkedIn benchmark cohort matches accounts by channel type and approximate follower count and includes only LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer.
entries.verbatim: - **What counts as a "similar account"?** The cohort is matched on two things: channel type (pages are compared to pages, profiles to profiles) and approximate follower count. It's scoped to other LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer — not LinkedIn as a whole.

entries.claim: By default, the All Channels Metrics chart displays the first 5 channels.
entries.verbatim: By default, in the **All Channels view,** the Metrics chart shows your **first 5 channels**.

entries.claim: Applying the channel filter makes the All Channels Metrics chart display up to 10 selected channels at a time.
entries.verbatim: Apply the channel filter at the top of the page, and the chart switches to your selected channels, drawing **up to 10** at a time.

entries.claim: When more channels exist than the chart can display, Insights shows an inline notice stating how many channels are shown.
entries.verbatim: When more channels exist than the chart can show, you'll see an inline notice (*"Showing X of Y channels. Filter by channel to see a different set."*) in the section subheading.

entries.claim: A selected channel is excluded from a chart when it does not report the metric being viewed, and Insights displays a notice.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** Some metrics aren't available for every channel. If a channel you've selected doesn't report the metric you're viewing, for example Pinterest doesn't report followers, you'll see a notice like "Pinterest profiles don't report followers, so they are excluded from this chart," and that channel won't be drawn.

entries.claim: The All Channels Metrics area contains two stacked cards: Followers above Posts.
entries.verbatim: The All Channels Metrics area is split into two stacked cards — **Followers** on top and **Posts** below.

entries.claim: The All Channels Followers metric offers By channel, Growth, and Over time views.
entries.verbatim: In the **All Channels** view, the **Followers** metric has its own view toggle so you can choose how to look at follower counts:

entries.claim: The By channel follower view is a ranked bar chart sorted by current followers, showing the lower starting or ending value as a solid base and period change as a colored segment.
entries.verbatim: - **By channel** — a ranked bar chart, one bar per channel, sorted by current followers. The solid base shows where you started or ended (whichever is lower), and the coloured segment on top shows the change for the period. The label at the top of the bar shows current followers and the change in brackets (e.g. "12,340 (+128)").

entries.claim: The Growth follower view is a gains-first diverging bar chart of net change, with green bars for gains and red bars for losses.
entries.verbatim: - **Growth** — a diverging bar chart of net change per channel, sorted gains-first. Bars are coloured by direction — green for gains, red for losses — so you can spot at a glance which channels grew and which shrank. The channel-colour legend isn't shown in this view because colour is being used to mean direction here.

entries.claim: The Over time follower view is a line or area chart of followers across the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Over time** — the standard line/area chart of followers across the period (this is the same view you've had before).

entries.claim: The Posts card in All Channels has its own view toggle.
entries.verbatim: Posts has its own toggle too — see **[Posts chart (All Channels)](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/using-insights-in-buffer-x4gLauQU5a#h-posts-chart-all-channels)** below.

entries.claim: The Followers chart shows a live number, an “As of [date]” carried-forward value, or “No data available” for each channel on a given day.
entries.verbatim: Hover over the Followers chart to see each channel's status for that day: a number for a live reading, "As of [date]" for a carried-forward value from the channel's most recent data, or "No data available" if the channel doesn't have a reading yet.

entries.claim: Dates before a channel was connected show “No data available” for that channel.
entries.verbatim: If you choose a date range that starts before a channel is connected, hovering over a date prior to connecting the channel will show "No data available" for the affected channel.

entries.claim: The All Channels Posts chart has Bar and Stacked Bar views.
entries.verbatim: Below the Followers table the Posts chart has its own **Bar / Stacked Bar** toggle:

entries.claim: The default Bar view ranks channels from most to fewest posts over the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: **Bar** (default) — a horizontal ranked chart, one bar per channel, showing total posts over the selected date range, sorted from most to fewest. Best for seeing at a glance which channel you posted to the most.

entries.claim: The Stacked Bar view displays vertical daily bars broken down by channel.
entries.verbatim: **Stacked Bar** — vertical bars over time, with each day broken down by channel. Best for seeing when you posted most across the range and how that activity splits across channels.

entries.claim: Share as Post on the Posts table captures the view currently on screen, including the ranked Bar view.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** ***Share as Post*** on the Posts table captures whichever view is on screen, including the ranked Bar view.

entries.claim: Share as Post on the Followers table captures only the Over Time chart, even from By channel or Growth.
entries.verbatim: This differs from the Followers table above, where ***Share as Post*** only captures the Over Time chart even if you're viewing **By channel** or **Growth**.

entries.claim: The Compare dropdown can overlay data from an earlier period and offers five comparison options.
entries.verbatim: Use the **Compare** dropdown to overlay data from an earlier period. Five options are available:

entries.claim: Previous Period compares against the same number of days immediately before the current date range.
entries.verbatim: **Previous Period** — the same number of days immediately before your current date range. Best for short-term trend checks (e.g. comparing this week to last week).

entries.claim: Same Period Last Month compares against the equivalent calendar window one month earlier.
entries.verbatim: **Same Period Last Month** — the equivalent calendar window one month earlier. Best for monthly reviews where month-over-month progress matters more than seasonality.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Year compares against the equivalent calendar window twelve months earlier.
entries.verbatim: **Same Period Last Year** — the equivalent calendar window twelve months earlier. Best for year-over-year reporting and tracking seasonal trends.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Week compares against the equivalent calendar window one week earlier.
entries.verbatim: **Same Period Last Week** — the equivalent calendar window one week earlier. Best for short-range, week-over-week check-ins. (Unavailable when your selected date range is longer than 7 days.)

entries.claim: Same Period Last Week is unavailable for selected date ranges longer than 7 days.
entries.verbatim: **Same Period Last Week** — the equivalent calendar window one week earlier. Best for short-range, week-over-week check-ins. (Unavailable when your selected date range is longer than 7 days.)

entries.claim: Custom comparison periods are available only on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: **Custom** (paid plans only) — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, cannot be selected.

entries.claim: A Custom comparison uses a historical window the same length as the current period.
entries.verbatim: **Custom** (paid plans only) — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, cannot be selected.

entries.claim: Custom comparison dates cannot overlap the current period or be in the future.
entries.verbatim: **Custom** (paid plans only) — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, cannot be selected.

entries.claim: The chart can display only the current period as a solid line.
entries.verbatim: **This Period** — shows only your current date range (solid line).

entries.claim: The chart can display only the comparison period as a dashed line.
entries.verbatim: **Comparison** — shows only the comparison period (dashed line).

entries.claim: The chart can overlay the current and comparison periods.
entries.verbatim: **Both** — overlays both periods on the same chart.

entries.claim: Hovering over a period toggle shows the exact date range it covers.
entries.verbatim: Hover over any toggle option to see a tooltip with the exact date range it covers, so you always know which window is which.

entries.claim: A comparison selection is saved in the URL and can be bookmarked or shared.
entries.verbatim: Your comparison choice is saved in the URL, so you can bookmark or share a specific view.

entries.claim: Channel and Tags filters can be combined to analyze a content category across selected channels.
entries.verbatim: 💡 **Tip:** Combine the channel filter with the Tags filter to see how a specific content category performed across your selected channels.

entries.claim: Takeaways provides AI-powered observations about recent content performance.
entries.verbatim: The Takeaways section provides AI-powered observations about your recent content performance.

entries.claim: Takeaways is not affected by the date range selector.
entries.verbatim: Unlike the Summary and Metrics chart, Takeaways are not affected by the date range selector. They reflect a broader view of your content performance and stay consistent as you explore different time windows in the chart above.

entries.claim: All Channels Takeaways includes cross-channel highlights such as channels with replies waiting and posts with no comments.
entries.verbatim: On the **All Channels** page, Takeaways works a little differently. Alongside the same kinds of cards you'd see on a single channel, you'll also get cross-channel highlights — like which channels have replies waiting or which posts got no comments — plus a curated mix of standout takeaways pulled from your individual channels.

entries.claim: All Channels Takeaways includes a curated mix of standout takeaways from individual channels.
entries.verbatim: Alongside the same kinds of cards you'd see on a single channel, you'll also get cross-channel highlights — like which channels have replies waiting or which posts got no comments — plus a curated mix of standout takeaways pulled from your individual channels.

entries.claim: All Channels Takeaways links to the full single-channel Insights page.
entries.verbatim: Each of these links out to the full single-channel Insights page if you want to dig deeper.

entries.claim: Takeaways calculates engagement rate by pooling engagement and reach across posts before calculating the rate.
entries.verbatim: **Note on engagement rate in Takeaways:** Takeaways calculates engagement rate by pooling engagement and reach across your posts first, then computing the rate — so posts seen by more people carry proportionally more weight than posts with only a handful of views.

entries.claim: Takeaways’ engagement-rate calculation gives posts with more reach proportionally more weight.
entries.verbatim: **Note on engagement rate in Takeaways:** Takeaways calculates engagement rate by pooling engagement and reach across your posts first, then computing the rate — so posts seen by more people carry proportionally more weight than posts with only a handful of views.

entries.claim: Takeaways counts Instagram saves and LinkedIn comments as engagement.
entries.verbatim: This calculation also counts Instagram saves and LinkedIn comments as engagement.

entries.claim: Performance tips identify patterns such as resonating formats, engagement-driving topics, and trends worth repeating.
entries.verbatim: **Performance tips** highlight patterns in your content — things like which formats are resonating, what topics are driving engagement, and trends worth repeating.

entries.claim: Repost suggestions identify high-performing older posts and suggest republishing them.
entries.verbatim: **Repost suggestions** identify your best-performing older posts and suggest republishing them to extend their reach.

entries.claim: A Start with AI card opens the post composer with the AI Assistant active and a performance-based prompt pre-filled.
entries.verbatim: **Start with AI cards** are interactive. Click one to open the post composer with the AI Assistant panel already active and a prompt pre-filled based on what's been working for you.

entries.claim: Users can edit or run a pre-filled Start with AI prompt and schedule the resulting post.
entries.verbatim: You can tweak the prompt or run it as-is, then schedule the resulting post like any other.

entries.claim: Draft reminders link to an unpublished draft and appear only when a channel has at least one draft.
entries.verbatim: **Draft reminders** point you back to a draft you have not published yet. They only show when your channel has at least one draft.

entries.claim: Draft reminders flag the newest draft when it is past its due date.
entries.verbatim: If the newest draft is past its due date, you’ll see a nudge that it’s overdue.

entries.claim: Review draft opens the composer so the draft can be finished and published.
entries.verbatim: You can click ***Review draft*** to open the composer and finish publishing.

entries.claim: The repost takeaway appears only for channels with posts older than four weeks.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** The repost takeaway only appears for channels with posts older than four weeks and is not currently available for Bluesky or Mastodon channels.

entries.claim: The repost takeaway is not currently available for Bluesky or Mastodon channels.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** The repost takeaway only appears for channels with posts older than four weeks and is not currently available for Bluesky or Mastodon channels.

entries.claim: Each Takeaway card has thumbs-up and thumbs-down feedback buttons.
entries.verbatim: Each Takeaway card has a thumbs-up and thumbs-down button in its header.

entries.claim: Takeaway feedback is used to tune the kinds of Takeaways shown in the future.
entries.verbatim: Click thumbs up if a takeaway felt useful, or thumbs down if it didn't — your feedback helps us tune which kinds of Takeaways you'll see in future.

entries.claim: A Takeaway feedback selection remains highlighted and can be unselected by clicking again.

objections.objection: “The Free plan is enough, so there is no reason to start paying.”
objections.answer: Free covers up to three channels and ten queued posts per channel. Paid plans become materially different when the buyer needs unlimited scheduling, unlimited history, custom analytics, reports, hashtag management, first-comment scheduling, or team approvals. Whether those additions justify the price for a light user is not established.

objections.objection: “If I upgrade, I have to pay for every connected channel, including the ones I was already using free.”
objections.answer: The evidence confirms this objection rather than resolving it: upgrading means paying for every connected channel. Annual billing provides a 20% discount, and channels above ten have lower per-channel rates, but there is no evidence of a paid-plan allowance for the first three channels.

provenance.quote: If you decide to upgrade to a paid plan, you will pay for each channel — including any channels you had while on the Free plan.

objections.objection: “I cannot trust client reports if Buffer's figures differ from the native platforms or some networks omit metrics.”
objections.answer: No supplied evidence fully resolves this objection. Buffer explicitly says metrics vary by network and numbers may differ from native analytics because platforms calculate and update data differently.

objections.objection: “The analytics and engagement coverage is inconsistent across channel types, so one dashboard will not really replace native tools.”
objections.answer: No supplied evidence fully resolves this objection. The compatibility evidence confirms that advanced analytics, engagement, automatic publishing, and historical backfill vary by network and account type; Google Business Profiles are excluded from Insights.

objections.objection: “Connecting client accounts will be a permissions headache, and expired access tokens will create ongoing maintenance.”
objections.answer: The evidence documents the required roles and connection process, but does not remove the maintenance burden: Facebook requires Full control, LinkedIn Pages require Super Admin status, YouTube requires the Owner, and access tokens can expire and require reconnection.

objections.objection: “I will not put client work into it until I can control who sees, drafts, and approves each channel.”
objections.answer: The Team plan includes unlimited users, approval workflows, and custom channel access and permissions. Users with Approval Required access can submit posts for review, while owners, admins, and Full Posting users can approve them.

objections.objection: “I do not want to enter a card for a trial and risk an unwanted charge.”
objections.answer: A buyer can start the Free plan without a trial or credit card. For a paid-plan trial, an account without payment details is automatically downgraded to Free rather than charged, although channels above the Free limit may be locked.

objections.objection: “The Team plan is wasteful for a solo operator; I only need better scheduling and analytics.”
objections.answer: Essentials is the solo paid option: it retains one user while adding unlimited scheduled posts, advanced analytics, reports, hashtag management, and first-comment scheduling. Team is primarily justified when unlimited users, access controls, approvals, or branded reports are needed.

objections.objection: “AI suggestions and takeaways may produce generic content that does not sound like me or understand my audience.”
objections.answer: The evidence shows that prompts can be edited before use and that Takeaway cards accept feedback, but it provides no customer proof that AI-generated posts consistently preserve a buyer's voice or improve business outcomes.
